title: Financial SLA‑compliant routing policy for preemptible vs guaranteed GPUs
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Enterprise customers need predictable spend for inference while still benefiting from cheaper preemptible (spot) capacity. Current router makes binary decisions (prefer spot when available, fall back to on‑demand) which causes cost surges when spot pools evict and latency SLOs are missed. This ticket defines a financial SLA‑aware routing policy that enforces tenant budget caps, chooses GPU classes by marginal cost/latency tradeoff, and degrades model variants gracefully when spend headroom is exhausted.

Scope: Implement routing controller logic, config surface in routing policy (tenant budget caps, soft vs hard caps, preemptible hedging factor), model variant degradation chain, and observability for financial SLOs. This does not include tenant billing UI changes (separate PM work).
acceptance_criteria: Configurable tenant budget cap enforced at request-time with soft-warning and hard-block behaviors
Router selects GPU class by policy that factors estimated tokens, per-token unit cost for instance class, and predicted latency impact
Hedged allocation across >=2 spot pools with probabilistic preemptible risk budget to limit expected evictions
Automatic fallback chain: preferred model variant -> lower-cost quantized variant -> smaller architecture -> on‑demand GPU; each step records a deterministic reason code
End-to-end tests demonstrating: (a) cost under cap for synthetic high-throughput traffic; (b) <5% increased latency p95 during controlled spot eviction simulation when hedging enabled
Dashboard + alerts showing spend vs cap, eviction rate, fallback frequency, and per-tenant cost-per-token
proposed_solution:
We will implement a risk‑aware allocator in the routing layer that attaches a short-lived budget context to each request. The allocator computes an expected cost vector for candidate placement options: (region, instance_class, spot/on‑demand, model_variant). Each option is scored by a utility function: utility = alpha*(1/estimated_latency) + beta*(budget_headroom_normalized) - gamma*(eviction_risk_score).

To limit spot exposure, tenants declare two numbers: soft_cap (alerts + progressive degradation) and hard_cap (reject or require approval). We maintain a per-tenant spot_risk_budget (tokens of acceptable eviction exposure) computed from historical evictions and chosen hedging factor. For multi-request workloads we use bounded hedging: break large batches across different spot pools and reserve a small on‑demand headroom for urgent requests.

Model degradation is explicit: each model on the catalog has an ordered fallback list with estimated latency and quality deltas. Router picks the cheapest option that keeps expected quality above tenant-defined floor. All decisions log reason_code and cost_estimate for post-hoc reconciliation.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Feature flag gated implementation + unit tests, add policy config API
Week 2: Integration tests with spot-eviction simulator (local runbook) and canary for internal tenants (10% traffic)
Week 3: Expand canary to 50% for non-critical tenants, enable dashboard metrics and alerts, gather telemetry
Week 4: Enable soft_caps by default for newly onboarded tenants, document escape hatches, begin gradual opt-in for existing tenants
Contingency: immediate rollback to existing cost-preference policy via feature flag if eviction-induced latency regressions > 10% p95
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hedging increases cross-region egress and could push cost up. Mitigation: include egress penalty in utility function and prefer same-region pools when cost-delta < threshold.
Risk: Incorrect cost estimates during volatile spot pricing. Mitigation: conservative smoothing window for spot price signal and rapid safety fallback to on‑demand headroom.
Risk: Tenant dissatisfaction when quality degrades under soft caps. Mitigation: opt-in messaging, per-tenant quality floors, and per-route override for critical routes.
Risk: Complexity in billing reconciliation. Mitigation: log deterministic cost_estimate for each routed request and add a reconciliation job to compare estimates to actual invoice lines.
Risk: State explosion if we track per-request budgets. Mitigation: use sliding-window aggregated tokens and probabilistic counters instead of strict per-request ledger where possible.
